expl: The book ‘On the Origin of Species’ was written by Charles Darwin. Charles Darwin was an English naturalist and biologist. The theory of evolution presented by him is called Darwinism or the Theory of Natural Selection.

stem: The reason for large-scale diversity among the organisms is –
expl: The group of scientists who gave a modern form to the theory of natural selection is called “Neo-Darwinists”. According to modern Neo-Darwinists, new organisms are formed after small changes in genes, due to which diversity increases in organisms. These changes are called “mutations”. Therefore, the main reason for very high diversity in living organisms is mutation.

stem: According to recent proof, the life on earth emerged approximately -
expl: According to the modern concept, the origin of life on the Earth occurred about 2,000 million (2,000,000,000) years ago. However, the oldest fossils are about 3,600 million years old. Important early fossils are considered to be remains of stromatolites (Stromatolites), which were a group of unicellular organisms. About 2,000 million years ago, eukaryotic cells originated, from which all living organisms of the present living world (except bacteria) were formed.

stem: latest ancestor of modern human is
expl: Cro-Magnon man anatomically similar to modern humans. He lived in the Stone Age and used bone tools. He had the ability to stitch and wear animal skins. He lived in caves, and his wall paintings are found on cave walls. He is the most recent prehistoric human.

stem: The main factor of development is -
expl: Today, the most accepted theory of evolution is known as the Modern Synthetic Theory of Evolution. In it, the origin (emergence) of species is explained on the basis of interactions of genetic variations and natural selection. In the process of natural selection, the beneficial traits of well-adapted organisms are inherited by the next generations, as a result species gradually change over time.

The most accepted theory of evolution is the Synthetic Theory of Evolution. In it, the origin of species can be understood on the basis of interactions of genetic variations and natural selection; that is, adaptation from generation to generation is the cause of evolution.
